authorization: User: etymologise all Indo-Aryan SIL surveys jointly; do everything; surface tough/unclear cases for audit once done.

proposals.evidence: Platts p. 295 gives Persian piyāz “onion”; the visually checked Hindi table has प्याज, independently supporting the existing Hindi pyaj donor. Survey piaj/pjaj and z/j/s adaptations belong to this regional loan family. The borrowed edge identifies a provisional Hindi/Urdu route; it does not assert direct Persian contact for each target. Existing Hindi pyaj “onion” is the provisional donor, under the user’s preference to link supported cross-IA families. An intermediate Indo-Aryan language or another lending locality remains possible; the attestation locality is not claimed as the historical lending site.

proposals.evidence: The existing Rohili Hindi ṭamaṭar tomato attestation is independently supported by the visually checked primary Hindi table, PDF page 11 item 3 टमाटर. The selected r-ending survey forms preserve this whole regional loan word, with vowel and dental/retroflex transcription differences retained. Forms resembling a separate direct tomato adaptation without final r are not included. Existing Hindi ṭamaṭar “tomato” is the provisional donor, under the user’s preference to link supported cross-IA families. An intermediate Indo-Aryan language or another lending locality remains possible; the attestation locality is not claimed as the historical lending site.
